title: Paging through ZCC lists with the Python SDK

prose.text: Most ZCC v1 lists return a bare JSON array, and the Python response object walks it with `has_next()` and `next()` on page-fullness guesses alone. {{app-profiles-envelope}} The Go helpers are in [[zcc.sdk-go.paging-and-requests]].

prose.label: Page size.
prose.text: {{list-devices-docstring-size}} The contract's own default and maximum are [[zcc.api.devices-wire:api-page-size]]. The key goes on the wire camel-cased: [[zcc.api.conventions:query-params-camel]] {{wrapper-zcc-limits}} {{limit-clamp-local-only}} {{oversized-page-size-sent}} {{no-default-size-sent}} {{zero-page-size}}

prose.label: Limits of the heuristic.
prose.text: {{no-loop-guard}} Whether every ZCC v1 list endpoint honours `page` and `pageSize` is open {{gap:page-param-honored}}. Client-side filtering of a page is [[shared.sdk-python.response-handling:search-current-page]].

checks.do: Whether the caller looped on `has_next()` and `next()`, and capped the loop and checked for repeated pages, since nothing in the SDK stops a server that ignores `page`.
Whether a `page_size` above 5000 or of 0 was passed, since it is sent as given.
Whether a `next()` that returned None meant an empty page rather than an error, by checking the error slot.

app-profiles-envelope.statement: The application-profiles list returns a `policies` envelope, which `get_application_profiles` unwraps itself.

quotes: def get_application_profiles(self, query_params: Optional[dict] = None) -> APIResult[dict]:
result = [ApplicationProfile(item) for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]

list-devices-docstring-size.statement: The `list_devices` docstring gives a default page size of 50 and a maximum of 5000.

evidence.after: def list_devices(self, query_params: Optional[dict] = None) -> APIResult[List[Device]]:

wrapper-zcc-limits.statement: The Python response object's page-size table gives ZCC a default of 50, a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 5000.

oversized-page-size-sent.statement: So a `page_size` above the ZCC maximum is sent unchanged as `pageSize`; the clamp changes only the response object's own continuation limit.
oversized-page-size-sent.conditions: Rests on the clamp running in the response constructor after fire_request, and on a read of the whole of _prepare_params at the pin finding no page-size check outside the ZPA branch; not observed on the wire.

limit-clamp-local-only.statement: A caller-supplied page size is clamped into that range by `validate_page_size`, which the response object runs when it is built, storing the result as its own `_limit`; `execute` builds that object only after `fire_request` has sent the request. Outside the ZPA branch, `_prepare_params` camel-cases the query parameters and drops `microtenantId`.

quotes: def validate_page_size(self, page_size: Optional[int], service_type: str) -> Optional[int]:

limits = self.SERVICE_PAGE_LIMITS.get(service_type, {}) max_page_size = limits.get("max", 100) min_page_size = limits.get("min", 1) validated_size = min(max(int(page_size), min_page_size), max_page_size) logger.debug("Validated page size: %d (user provided: %s)", validated_size, page_size) return validated_size

evidence.after: # Normal param conversion if not ZPA

no-default-size-sent.statement: When the caller gives no page size the SDK sends none, on the first request or on later pages, and the API's own default applies.

quotes: # Don't set any default - let the API use its own default behavior

zero-page-size.statement: An explicit `page_size` of 0 is sent as `pageSize=0`, but the response object reads its limit with an `or` chain, so it treats 0 as no size given and pages as if the size were omitted.

evidence.after: # Normal param conversion if not ZPA

flat-array-fix.statement: Since release 1.9.42 (PR 564) a ZCC flat JSON array is not marked as a complete, unpaged response, so `has_next()` and `next()` can walk a list such as `list_devices`.

quotes: Fixed ZCC pagination so `has_next()`/`next()` properly traverse all pages on flat-array list endpoints (e.g. `list_devices`).

page-seeds-counter.statement: A `page` the caller passes on a ZCC list seeds the response object's page counter, so `next()` asks for the page after it. Any integer is accepted, including 0 or a negative number.

quotes: if self._service_type == "zcc" and "page" in self._params: try: self._page = int(self._params["page"]) except Exception: self._page = 1 # Resolve the user-supplied page size from the correct param key per service.

zcc-next-branch.statement: `next()` tests the service type for zdx, zcell, zia and ziam in turn, so ZCC (service type `zcc`) takes the final else branch: it adds one to the page counter, sets `page`, and resends the original query parameters.

quotes: if not self._has_next(): logger.debug("No more pages to fetch") return [], None if self._service_type == "zdx": logger.debug("[DEBUG] Taking ZDX pagination branch.") self._params["offset"] = self._next_offset elif self._service_type == "zcell": logger.debug("[DEBUG] Taking ZCell pagination branch.")

# ZCell pages are 0-based: the first (un-paginated) request returns # page 0. The internal _page counter is 1-based, so the API page # index is _page - 1 (e.g. _page == 2 -> page=1, the second page). self._page += 1 self._params["page"] = self._page - 1 elif self._service_type == "zia":

logger.debug("[DEBUG] Taking ZIA pagination branch.") self._page += 1 self._params["page"] = self._page # Only set pageSize if user explicitly provided it (don't override API defaults) if self._limit and "pageSize" not in self._params: self._params["pageSize"] = self._limit

logger.debug(f"[DEBUG] _fetch_next_page params for ZIA: {self._params}") elif self._service_type == "ziam": logger.debug("[DEBUG] Taking ZIAM pagination branch.") if self._next_link: from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse parsed_url = urlparse(self._next_link) query_params = parse_qs(parsed_url.query)

for key, value in query_params.items(): self._params[key] = value[0] if len(value) == 1 else value self._url = f"{parsed_url.scheme}://{parsed_url.netloc}{parsed_url.path}" logger.debug(f"[DEBUG] _fetch_next_page params for ZIAM: {self._params}") else: logger.debug("[DEBUG] Taking ZPA/other pagination branch.")

has-next-first-page.statement: After the first page, `has_next()` is true whenever that page held any item, even a page shorter than the requested size. A ZCC response that is a single object is held as a one-item list, so it counts as a non-empty page too.

evidence.after: # ZCC can return either a single object or a list of objects

has-next-later-pages.statement: On later pages, with a page size given, `has_next()` is true only when the last page was at least that size; without one, any non-empty page continues, so the walk stops only after a request returns an empty page.

evidence.after: # If user provided limit, only continue if last page was "full"
quotes: # This may result in one extra empty API call, but respects API defaults
# Subsequent pages - if no explicit limit, use heuristic based on results returned
# If we got results, try one more page. The next call will return empty and stop.

no-loop-guard.statement: Nothing in the response object detects a repeated page or caps the number of pages, so if an endpoint ignores `page` and returns the same full page each time, `has_next()` stays true and a loop on it does not end.
no-loop-guard.conditions: Read from oneapi_response.py, which keeps only the page counter, item counts and the last page; no endpoint was observed ignoring `page`.

page-param-honored.title: Whether every ZCC v1 list endpoint honours page and pageSize
page-param-honored.blocks: trusting a drained Python or Go list as the complete inventory
page-param-honored.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the Python traversal is a client heuristic, not a backend guarantee, and endpoint-specific tenant behavior should be validated. Among lists, the contract documents `page` and `pageSize` with a default and a maximum together only on `getDevices`; `application-profiles` documents a default of 50 alone. Most v1 lists carry no total or page-count metadata, but the contract gives `application-profiles`, `getZdxGroupEntitlements` and `getZpaGroupEntitlements` a `totalCount`, and the Go SDK decodes a `totalCount` from the v1 trusted-network list. On a tenant with more records than one page, list each v1 endpoint with a small `pageSize` and pages 1, 2 and 3, and compare the IDs.

expect.description: Specifies the total number of policies in the database related to search criteria.

expect.name: pageSize
expect.description: Specifies the page size. The default size is 50.
